title.description: Display title. Absent on every project created before it existed.

commerceStoreStructure.description:
The discovered Commerce store hierarchy — websites, store groups and store views, each with its `code` AND its human `name`.

The pickers show the user "CitiSignal Store"; only `citisignal_store` was ever kept, so every later surface made them translate. The structure is the one thing that holds both, and it was fetched and thrown away on every discovery. Persisting it turns a name into an offline lookup BY CODE on any surface — which is also why nothing has to pair a name with a code defensively: the code IS the lookup key, so a name can never land on the wrong one.

A CATALOG, not a selection: refreshed wholesale whenever discovery runs. Absent until it has run once (every project predating this) — consumers then show the bare code, which is a correct rendering, not a degraded one.

appBuilderComponents.description: Keyed appBuilderComponent state — THE single source of truth for mesh + integration deploy state (Model B; the plan/ADR call this concept a "deployable" — `appBuilderComponent` is the shipped name). Persisted in the manifest (D3 Step 01) and, since D3 Step 07 retired the singular write-side, the only written model; the legacy singletons above are read-only migration inputs. See docs/architecture/adr/011-app-builder-deployables.md.

demo.description: The storefront row for a project built on an added demo (D2): the demo's description and its repository. Read before the catalog by `resolveStorefrontForProject`; absent for a project on a shipped brand.

organizationName.description: Human-readable org name (for display; the token can't resolve it when wrong)

workspaceName.description: Human-readable workspace name — written by the wizard and read back by `useWizardState`; the type simply never declared it.

commerceProfile.description:
The Adobe product profile this project's credentials use for Commerce (ACCS-REST-API), with the Commerce tenant it was chosen for.

Adobe's org catalog answers that service with no profiles at all now and then — twenty minutes of it on 2026-09-21, and a whole failed add on 2026-09-22 — while the entitlement is intact. Remembering what was chosen lets a later workspace subscribe anyway. The TENANT is what makes it safe: a project pointed at another Commerce instance must never be handed this.

websites.description: All websites in the Commerce instance

storeGroups.description: All store groups across all websites

storeViews.description: All store views across all store groups

CommerceStoreStructure.description: Complete Commerce store hierarchy fetched from REST API. Contains all websites, store groups, and store views.

code.description: Website code used in storefront configuration (e.g., 'base', 'citisignal')

CommerceWebsite.description: Commerce website — top-level entity that owns payment, shipping, tax, and pricing config. Maps to REST API: GET /V1/store/websites

website_id.description: Parent website ID — used for cascading filters

root_category_id.description: Root category ID assigned to this store group

CommerceStoreGroup.description:
Commerce store group — intermediate entity that owns root category. Maps to REST API: GET /V1/store/storeGroups

Property names match the Commerce REST API response format (snake_case).

code.description: Store view code used in storefront configuration (e.g., 'citisignal_us')

store_group_id.description: Parent store group ID — used for cascading filters

website_id.description: Grandparent website ID — denormalized for convenience

is_active.description: Whether this store view is active. Commerce's REST API sends the integers 1/0, not booleans — read from a real bodea manifest 2026-08-23, after the boolean-only declaration had every project load warning "is_active must be boolean" three times per view. Consumers check truthiness, which both shapes satisfy.

CommerceStoreView.description:
Commerce store view — leaf entity representing a language/locale. Maps to REST API: GET /V1/store/storeViews

Property names match the Commerce REST API response format (snake_case).

LegacyManifestMeshState.description: Legacy singular mesh state, MANIFEST-ONLY since PL-1 phase 2 — the in-memory `Project` no longer carries it. Read solely by the quarantined read-migration (`appBuilderComponentMigration`), which folds it into the keyed map on every load.

LegacyManifestAppState.description: Legacy singular app state, MANIFEST-ONLY since PL-1 phase 2 (see above).

status.description: `'deploying'` is TRANSIENT: written when a deploy starts so pollers (agents reading get_project, the grid) can tell an in-flight run from a stale prior outcome — the previous error used to sit there looking current for the whole deploy (measured 2026-08-27, seven minutes of misleading polling). Always overwritten by the final outcome; a crash mid-deploy leaves it behind, which reads as "still deploying" until the next deploy or verify corrects it.

commerceAppId.description:
The id this component declares to Commerce (App Management apps only, and only for a COPY — the first of a kind keeps the id its app ships with).

Written the first time the copy deploys and never rewritten: Commerce names its webhooks and events from it and refuses to change it on an upgrade, so a later rename moves the label and leaves this alone (`commerceAppId.ts`).

name.description: Display name for the integration (durable home for the user-facing name).

catalogId.description: The catalog entry this component was made from, when its id is not that entry's id: a second copy of a kind the project already holds (`demo-erp-2`). ABSENT means the id IS the catalog id — every component before this, and the first of each kind. Read through `catalogEntryFor`.

error.description:
Why the last deploy failed — set with `status: 'error'`, cleared by the next non-error outcome (see `recordDeployOutcome`).

Without it a failed component persisted the fact of failure and none of the reason, so the card read "Deploy failed" / MESH ERROR and the only way to learn more was to run the deploy again and watch the logs. Redacted and first-line-only via `sanitizeErrorForLogging` before it lands here: this is persisted to the project manifest on disk, so raw CLI output must not be.

providesEnvVars.description: Resolved provided values another appBuilderComponent consumes (e.g. { MESH_ENDPOINT }).

at.description: ISO date string of the attempt.

version.description: The app version installed in Commerce (its manifest's `metadata.version`), when known.

needsReinstall.description: The installed app cannot be upgraded in place; a reinstall would apply the new version.

installation.description: App Management install outcome (lifecycle 'app-management' apps only). Written after every deploy's automatic install/associate pass; `detail` carries the no-op reason on skip or the hands-back line on failure. A failed install does NOT mark the deploy failed — the app is deployed, merely dormant until installed (Commerce Admin > Apps > App Management).

commit.description: The branch head on GitHub, when the branch moved.

version.description: The version in the clone, when it differs from the installed one.

checkedAt.description: ISO date string of the check.

updateAvailable.description: Newer code is available: the source branch on GitHub has commits the clone lacks, or the clone's app version differs from the one installed in Commerce. Set by the integrations screen's check, removed by a successful update (integrationUpdateCheck).

workspace.description:
The Adobe workspace this component is deployed into.

**ABSENT means the project's own workspace** (`project.adobe`), which is what every component created before AB-23 has and what every component still gets until the add path starts creating one. That default is the whole reason this is optional: existing projects keep working with no migration.

The `id` is what deploys target. The `name` is Adobe's machine name, which an App Management install sends (`buildAppData`) and which CANNOT be changed after the workspace is created — Adobe answers `400 "Workspace name can not be changed"` — so it is recorded here rather than looked up or derived.

systems.description: The systems this integration uses (their `appBuilderComponents` ids), written when the pair is added. Read through `appBuilderComponentLinks`.

usedBy.description: The integration this system belongs to (its `appBuilderComponents` id).

removalStopped.description: Why the last removal stopped before undeploying, in plain words: a clean-up only the deployed code can do did not finish. The card offers Remove anyway. Gone with the record when a removal finishes.

envVars.description: Env vars at last deploy — the staleness baseline (mesh kind).

userDeclinedUpdate.description: User clicked "Later" on the redeploy prompt (mesh kind).

declinedAt.description: ISO date string when the user declined (mesh kind).

AppBuilderComponentState.description: Keyed appBuilderComponent state (Model B). One concept replaces the singular `meshState` + `appState`. The mesh's endpoint + staleness fields and an integration's URL(s) live here.

AppBuilderComponentKind.description: An App Builder component's kind: a mesh artifact, an App Builder integration, or a SYSTEM — a stand-in for an external system an integration talks to (the demo ERP). A system is a plain App Builder app with no Commerce install; it never gets a card of its own and comes and goes with the integration it is bound to (`AppBuilderComponentCatalogEntry.boundTo`; decision 13, 2026-09-14).

configFlags.description: Storefront config.json public flags injected for this package (e.g., commerce-b2b-enabled). Merged into config.public.default by the config generator — data-driven, mirrors addon configFlags.

requiresMesh.description:
API Mesh requirement for this package.
- true: mesh auto-included, no user choice
- false (default): no mesh, no user choice
- 'optional': mesh toggle shown, user decides

datapack.description: The datapack this demo expects (D26). The Sample Data step pre-selects it and says why; the SC can change it. Optional: shipped brands may leave the choice open.

integrations.description: Integrations this demo depends on (D29). The Integrations area starts with them added; the SC can remove any. The same field a shared-demo description file carries, so the catalog and the slice cannot drift.

description.description: Optional here and below; `DemoPackage` requires them because a shipped brand always has a card and store codes.

configDefaults.description: Default configuration values (env var name to value) - embedded brand data

storefrontKind.description: Read from the repository when the demo was added, never from the description file.

AddedDemo.description: The stored storefront row for a project built on an added demo (D2): the slice plus where it came from and what kind it is. Every post-creation lookup resolves this before the catalog.

DatapackReference.description: A datapack a demo expects (D26). `version` absent means the catalog's default rule.

DemoIntegrations.description: Integrations a demo depends on (D29): catalog ids, and custom apps by link.

CustomIntegrationSource.description: A custom App Builder app by GitHub coordinates, the `appBuilderComponentSources` shape.

indexPath.description: Where the site lists its pages. Required: whoever names a content site names its index path (the catalog, the project row, a description file); only the Add a demo package probe looks one up, for a repository that names no site of its own, and records what it found. `contentIndex.ts` builds the URL every reader uses.

StorefrontKind.description: The two kinds of storefront a repository can hold.

name.description: User-provided display name (pre-filled from repo name)

CustomBlockLibrary.description: A user-provided block library from a GitHub URL

AddonSource.description:
AddonSource - GitHub repository source for an addon

Used by addons that fetch content from an external repository (e.g., the Commerce Block Collection fetches blocks from isle5).

pinned.description: When true: the prompt lives in globalState and appears in every project; render-time sort floats it above unpinned prompts. When falsy: project-scoped, visible only in the current project.

AiPrompt.description:
AiPrompt - A user-saved AI prompt

Storage is scope-routed by the `pinned` field. Pinned prompts persist in VS Code globalState under `demoBuilder.ai.globalPrompts` and appear in every project. Unpinned prompts persist in the current project's `.demo-builder.json` manifest under `Project.aiPrompts` and stay project-specific. Toggling pin moves the prompt across stores.

Legacy data: prompts pinned before the global-pin feature shipped remain in their project's manifest until the user manually unpins then re-pins them — no automatic migration.

Array order within either store is preserved; render-time pinned-first sort happens in the UI layer.
